newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors enter Japan DKB Bank in apparent raid.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors enter Japan DKB Bank in apparent raid.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors entered the headquarters of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) on Tuesday in what appeared to be a raid in connection with the widening Nomura Securities racketeer payoff scandal.
A DKB spokesman said some 100 officers from the Tokyo Prosecutors' Office had entered through the main reception area of the headquarters building, but they could not confirm the purpose of the move.

DKB, one of Japan's top commercial banks, on Monday declined comment on domestic media reports that it was being questioned by prosecutors over alleged questionable loans to a racketeer at the centre of a scandal at Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Japan's largest brokerage. DKB said it could not comment on deals with individual customers.

The daily Mainichi Shimbun reported earlier that the bank had been questioned over its loans to "sokaiya" Ryuichi Koike, a principal figure in the Nomura scandal. Koike and his younger brother Yoshinori Koike were arrested last Thursday on suspicion of violating Japan's Commercial Code by taking some 50 million yen ($434,000) in illegal payments from Nomura.
Two former Nomura executives and a third senior Nomura official have also been arrested in the case.
The Commercial Code bans companies from making payments to "sokaiya", racketeers who typically extort money from companies by threatening to disrupt shareholder meetings. ($1=115 yen)
